metadata.description: 🧬 THE RECOVERY KERNEL A systems-architecture framework for understanding addiction, behavior, biological bottlenecks, and recovery. Forkable. Global. Human-first. Insight, not instructions. Clarity, not prescriptions. Understanding, not judgment. The Problem Was Never That People Were Broken For generations, addiction has been explained through competing languages: moral failure , lack of willpower , disease , trauma , bad choices , genetics , environment , brain chemistry . Each of these lenses may contain part of the picture. But people are systems. Human behavior emerges from interactions between biology, environment, learning, memory, stress, reward, metabolism, expression, social context, and time. The Recovery Kernel was built to study those interactions together. It is an open-source systems framework for exploring the architecture behind addictive patterns and recovery. The central premise is simple: Do not begin with blame. Begin with architecture. 🎯 What Is The Recovery Kernel? The Recovery Kernel is a home-level biological and behavioral insight framework designed to help people explore: why addictive patterns may emerge; how those patterns become reinforced; why people can respond differently to similar substances or environments; how biology and lived experience may interact; where biological or behavioral bottlenecks may exist; and why recovery pathways can differ dramatically between individuals. The Kernel does not replace clinicians, therapists, laboratories, emergency services, or medical systems. It gives individuals another tool: a structured way to ask better questions. The framework brings together areas such as: 🧬 genetic architecture 🧠 neurochemical signaling and clearance 🔄 behavioral reinforcement loops 🌍 environmental conditioning 🧪 metabolism and pharmacology 🧫 epigenetic and regulatory factors 🎭 expressive and behavioral tendencies 🧩 lived experience and contextual signals The goal is not to reduce a human being to a gene, diagnosis, substance, or story. The goal is to construct a more complete map. 🧠 Why This Exists Most people trying to understand addiction are caught between three worlds. The clinical world Accurate information can be buried inside terminology that many people were never taught to interpret. The anecdotal world Forums and social media overflow with: “This worked for me.” “Take this.” “Never take that.” “You have exactly what I had.” Personal experience can be valuable. But one person's nervous system is not everyone else's nervous system. The lived world Then there is the person's actual experience: Why does this affect me differently? Why can that person stop and I cannot? Why do I repeat something I consciously want to stop? Why does my behavior change under stress? Why do I feel like three different versions of myself depending on my state? Why does the explanation I was given not seem to fit everything I experience? The Recovery Kernel exists in the space between these worlds. It provides a structured lens for asking: What interacting systems could produce this pattern? It is not a treatment. It is not a diagnosis. It is not a medical protocol. It is a framework for understanding. ⚙️ Addiction as a Systems Bottleneck Traditional narratives frequently isolate one explanation: the substance or the trauma or the genes or the environment or the behavior The Kernel asks a different question: What happens when several individually manageable constraints interact and become one reinforcing system? A simplified conceptual model might look like this: GENETIC ARCHITECTURE ↓ SIGNALING + CLEARANCE ↓ REWARD / STRESS RESPONSE ↕ ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONING ↕ BEHAVIORAL REINFORCEMENT ↕ MEMORY + EXPRESSION ↓ REPEATING SYSTEM STATE The point is not that every addictive pattern follows this exact sequence. The point is that human behavior is multivariable . The Kernel treats addictive patterns as possible system-level bottlenecks rather than evidence of bad character. 🪞 The Kernel Is a Mirror The Recovery Kernel is designed to help a person examine their own patterns without immediately converting observation into condemnation. It asks questions such as: What happened? Under what conditions? What changed before the behavior? Which state was the person in? Which signals are consistent? Which signals contradict one another? What information is missing? What could be biological? What could be environmental? What could be learned? What could be temporary? What requires professional investigation? The Kernel does not say: “You are broken.” It asks: “What architecture could explain what you are experiencing?” 🎭 Why Bias Matters Human testimony is extraordinarily valuable. It is also variable. People report their experiences from different system states: optimized states; dysregulated states; masked states; defensive states; performative states; confused states; fatigued states; intoxicated states; withdrawal states; socially filtered states. A person can minimize. A person can exaggerate. A person can forget. A person can reinterpret the past through the present. A person can answer with what they believe they should feel rather than what they actually felt. Sometimes people simply do not know which details are relevant. For this reason: Phenotype-first inference is probabilistic, not deterministic. The Kernel does not automatically treat testimony as objective truth. It treats testimony as signal . Expression is not dismissed as noise. Behavior is not automatically converted into diagnosis. Signals are considered: carefully, contextually, comparatively, and with explicit awareness of uncertainty. 🧬 Genomic Data: Powerful, but Optional The Recovery Kernel can be explored without genomic sequencing. In this mode, it operates as a probabilistic reasoning framework . It can help organize questions around: behavioral patterns; environmental triggers; family history; differential substance response; medication history; recurring states; tolerance patterns; recovery patterns; expressive tendencies. When high-quality genomic information is available, the framework can incorporate a more detailed architectural layer. Depending on the quality and type of data available, genomic analysis may examine areas including: metabolic pathways; receptor variants; transporter architecture; regulatory regions; methylation-related pathways; copy-number variation; pharmacogenomic markers; clearance pathways; signaling architecture. High-coverage whole-genome sequencing data can provide substantially more information than phenotype inference alone. But genomic information is not magical. It still requires interpretation. Genetics is not destiny. And the Kernel remains: educational, exploratory, and non-diagnostic. 🔬 What Makes The Recovery Kernel Different? Many recovery resources are primarily: Therapeutic 12-step programs, psychotherapy, CBT, counseling, group work, and related interventions. Anecdotal Stories and personal recommendations based on individual experience. Clinical Research papers, diagnostic manuals, pharmacology references, and professional medical systems. The Recovery Kernel occupies another layer. It is a systems-engineering model of human behavior. It was developed through an evolving collaboration involving: human design and lived observation; software systems; structured knowledge models; multiple artificial-intelligence systems; genomic and pharmacological reasoning frameworks; document libraries; translation systems; open-source iteration. Its philosophical orientation is: Move Away From Move Toward Moral judgment Systems understanding Shame Architecture Certainty without evidence Explicit uncertainty One-size-fits-all narratives Individual context Anecdotal absolutism Structured evidence Stigma Understanding “What is wrong with you?” “What happened in this system?” 🏠 What Can Someone Do With It at Home? The Kernel is intended to help people explore and understand . A person can use the framework to: 🧠 explore mechanisms that may contribute to addictive patterns; 🧬 examine possible relationships between biology and behavior; 🔁 map repeating behavioral loops; 🌍 identify environmental contexts associated with increased vulnerability; 🧪 better understand why substances may affect individuals differently; 📊 organize observations before speaking with professionals; 🔎 compare lived experience with clinical explanations; 💊 explore questions to discuss with pharmacists or physicians; 🧩 contextualize contradictory experiences; 🪞 examine behavior through a biological and systems lens rather than a moral one. It gives people insight, not instructions. Clarity, not prescriptions. Understanding, not treatment. 🌅 What This Gives People Before having a structured framework, many people experience: shame confusion contradictory advice anecdotal noise opaque clinical language fragmented explanations difficulty reconciling lived experience with expert opinion The Kernel attempts to replace that fragmentation with: a structured, bias-aware model; a vocabulary for discussing architecture; a way to organize observations; a method for evaluating competing explanations; a way to better prepare for conversations with professionals; a means of seeing tendencies without immediately converting them into identity; a way to remove unnecessary moral framing from biological and behavioral questions. For many people, the most important question is not: “What should I be called?” It is: “Why does this keep happening?” The Recovery Kernel was built around that question. 🔊 Built for the Global Dancefloor The Recovery Kernel was not built only for clinics, offices, or quiet rooms. It was also built with the global dancefloor in mind. For the person standing beneath a speaker stack at 4:00 in the morning. For the person flying home on Monday wondering why their friends seem fine and they do not. For the person who loves music, movement, travel, nightlife, community, and altered states — but wants to understand their own biology well enough to protect the life that makes those experiences possible. For DJs. For dancers. For bartenders. For promoters. For queer nightlife communities. For sober ravers. For people in recovery who still love electronic music. For people who do not identify with traditional recovery culture at all. For the friends who notice something is wrong before anyone else does. For the people who dance all night and still have to wake up inside the same nervous system the next morning. 🌍 The Communities We Had in Mind The Recovery Kernel is designed to be relevant to people electronic-music ecosystem. 🇦🇱 Albania UNUM Festival Kala Festival And the growing electronic-music communities of the Albanian Riviera. 🇬🇧 London Junction 2 Body Movements Along with London's house, ecosystem: International Music Summit — IMS Circoloco DC-10 and the island's international house and techno communities. 🇮🇱 Israel The country's electronic-music and psytrance communities, including festival communities such as Doof Festival , as well as the wider dance-music culture surrounding Tel Aviv and beyond. 🌎 And Beyond The Recovery Kernel is equally relevant to communities surrounding: Tomorrowland Sónar MUTEK and countless local festivals, warehouse parties, clubs, circuit events, beach gatherings, sound-system cultures, and underground dance communities around the world. 🎛️ Why the Dancefloor Matters Dance culture is often discussed from two extremes. One side says: Just say no. The other says: Everyone does it. You'll be fine. Neither statement contains enough information to describe a human nervous system. People attending the same event can have radically different experiences. The same substance does not necessarily produce the same response in every person. The same weekend does not produce the same recovery timeline. The same environment does not create the same risk. The same behavior does not emerge from the same architecture. The Recovery Kernel exists in that space. Not to tell people how to party. Not to pretend risk does not exist. Not to pretend nightlife is inherently pathological. And not to demand that people abandon music, community, sexuality, movement, travel, or celebration in order to deserve understanding. The question is: What does this particular human system need us to understand? 💃 Recovery Does Not Have to Mean Exile From Joy For some people, traditional recovery culture can feel like an instruction to disappear from the world they knew. Leave the music. Leave the friends. Leave the nightlife. Leave the dancefloor. Leave sexuality. Leave celebration. Leave every environment associated with the former self. Sometimes distance from a particular environment is necessary. Sometimes it is lifesaving. But the larger goal of recovery should not automatically be permanent exile from joy. A person may need to learn: what environments destabilize them; what biological vulnerabilities they carry; what substances create disproportionate risk; what behavioral loops precede loss of control; what social conditions increase vulnerability; what recovery actually feels like in their own nervous system; and how to build a life in which pleasure does not automatically become self-destruction. The Recovery Kernel is interested in that question. How does a person remain alive enough to keep hearing the music? How do they understand themselves well enough to know when the dancefloor is joy — and when it has become a warning? How do we help people return to life without demanding that life become colorless? That is why the dancefloor belongs inside the Recovery Kernel. Because recovery is not merely the absence of a substance. It is the return of a person to their own life. 🌍 A Global Framework Addiction does not speak one language. Neither should recovery information. The Recovery Kernel project has been developed around a principle of global accessibility, with multilingual documentation and audio resources forming part of the broader project. 🌐 Global & Regional English English — Global Australian English Indian English Nigerian Pidgin — Naijá 🌹 Romance Languages French Spanish — Castilian Mexican Spanish Brazilian Portuguese European Portuguese Italian Catalan Galician 🏔️ Germanic & Nordic Languages German — Hochdeutsch Dutch Swedish Norwegian — Bokmål Danish 🧭 Slavic, Uralic & Other European Languages Polish Czech Bosnian Greek Turkish Finnish Basque — Euskara Irish — Gaeilge 🕌 Middle East & Central Asia Arabic — Modern Standard Hebrew Persian / Farsi Dari 🌏 South & Southeast Asia Hindi Bengali Indonesian Malay Burmese Thai Vietnamese Filipino / Tagalog 🏯 East Asia Chinese — Simplified Japanese Korean 🌍 African Languages Afrikaans Zulu — isiZulu Xhosa — isiXhosa Swahili — Kiswahili Hausa Yoruba Igbo The broader project also includes multilingual audiobook distribution designed to make the material usable beyond the written page. 📚 A Growing Recovery Library The Recovery Kernel is more than one book. It is an evolving library of tools and frameworks addressing areas such as: neurogenomics; substance-specific education; harm reduction; pharmacological interactions; recovery pathways; behavioral architecture; community safety; embodied wellness; movement and dance; genomic diversity; biohacking education; pharmacogenomic questions; multilingual accessibility. The project has included guides addressing multiple substance categories and recovery contexts, along with special resources for community safety, genomic interpretation, and embodied wellness. 💃 Recovery Is Also Embodied Recovery is not merely an intellectual exercise. Human beings move. Dance. Breathe. Touch the ground. Hear rhythm. Form communities. Experience pleasure. The Recovery Kernel project recognizes that recovery can involve more than avoiding a substance. It can also involve learning how to inhabit life again. That is why the larger library includes material exploring: movement; rhythm; nervous-system regulation; grounding; community connection; celebration; joy; safer social environments. The purpose is not to create another culture of permanent punishment. It is to help make room for life. 🛠️ Tools & Resources 🧬 DNA Estimation Estimate a preliminary DNA-related profile without a physical test: https://tinyurl.com/eab3k3nf When completing phenotype-based estimation, consider answering from the state in which the relevant pattern was most strongly expressed rather than only from an optimized or recovered state. Remember: phenotype estimation is probabilistic and cannot substitute for actual genomic testing. ⚠️ Interaction Checker Explore prescription, substance-risk, and pharmacogenomic interaction information: https://tinyurl.com/3y47pwtw Interaction information should be used to support informed conversations with qualified medical professionals, pharmacists, and emergency services where appropriate. 🍹 The Mocktail Prescriber The project includes The Bartender's Friend Mocktail Prescriber , an experimental framework designed to connect personal profile information with functional, non-alcoholic beverage concepts. For best personalization, genomic information may provide additional input beyond phenotype estimation. 🧪 Peptide Advisor & BioHacker Routine Generator Peptide Advisor https://tinyurl.com/ms9msj78 BioHacker Edition https://tinyurl.com/2b2eykpd These tools are educational. Peptides and experimental biohacking compounds can involve meaningful uncertainty, quality-control concerns, contraindications, and medical risk. Clinical involvement and qualified medical guidance are strongly recommended. 🎧 Free Audiobook Editions The project includes free audiobook resources for people who: prefer listening; have difficulty reading long documents; are traveling; are exercising; have visual-accessibility needs; learn better through audio. YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@J.R.Token.TheArchitect Listen while walking. Listen while sitting outside. Listen while rebuilding. The format is less important than making the information accessible. 📖 Paperback Edition For people who prefer a physical book: https://amazon.com/dp/B0GCVGTWQ8 A physical edition offers an alternative to screens, mobile devices, consoles, and constant digital distraction. Read somewhere quiet. Sit outside. Breathe fresh air. Take what is useful. Leave what is not. Return when you are ready. ☕ Support the Project The Recovery Kernel is designed around open access and broad availability. People who find the project useful can support its continuation here: https://buymeacoffee.com/jrtoken Another form of support: Consider donating books or educational materials to local prisons, recovery communities, shelters, or other places where access to information is limited. Knowledge should not belong only to people with money, perfect insurance, a university login, or a stable life. 🧑‍💻 Open Source Philosophy The Recovery Kernel is built around: Transparency Models and assumptions should be visible enough to examine and challenge. Accessibility Useful knowledge should be understandable outside professional institutions. Dignity People deserve explanations that do not begin with humiliation. Forkability Communities should be able to adapt tools for their own contexts. Global Reach Language should not be a gatekeeper to understanding. Bias Awareness Human reports, datasets, models, and AI outputs all have limitations. Community Participation People with lived experience are not merely research subjects. Their observations can help reveal where existing models fail. Scientific Curiosity A framework must be allowed to evolve when better evidence appears. 🤝 Who Is This For? The project may be useful to: Individuals People attempting to understand their own patterns, biology, triggers, or recovery experience. Families and Supporters People trying to understand what someone they care about may be experiencing. Developers People interested in building accessible health-education, genomics, recovery, visualization, translation, or AI systems. Researchers People exploring neurogenomics, behavior, recovery diversity, environmental interaction, or computational models. Recovery Communities Groups looking for non-moralizing language and adaptable educational frameworks. Clinicians and Pharmacists Professionals interested in seeing the kinds of questions people are attempting to answer outside traditional systems. Translators and Accessibility Contributors People who can help make knowledge available across languages, cultures, literacy levels, and media formats. 🌎 Why I Am Sharing This A lot of people do not connect with traditional recovery language. Some feel judged. Some feel misunderstood. Some have heard the same explanation for years and still do not understand what is happening inside them. Some want language that explains the brain and body without adding moral weight. Some are simply trying to survive long enough to understand themselves. That is why I am sharing this. Not because one framework contains every answer. Not because every hypothesis will survive forever unchanged. Not because software can replace human care. I am sharing it because people deserve access to tools that help them ask better questions about their own lives. If one person finds clarity here, then sharing it was worth it. Take care of yourselves. Read what is useful to you right now. Come back to the rest when you are ready. 🌐 How This Changes the Lens The Recovery Kernel attempts to move the conversation: MORAL FAILURE → BIOLOGICAL + BEHAVIORAL ARCHITECTURE SHAME → UNDERSTANDING CONFUSION → STRUCTURED QUESTIONS ANECDOTE → EVIDENCE + CONTEXT STIGMA → CURIOSITY JUDGMENT → INVESTIGATION "YOU FAILED" → "WHAT HAPPENED IN THE SYSTEM?" This framework is intended to be: humane scientifically curious bias-aware systems-oriented empowering non-judgmental open to correction 🔭 The Larger Vision Imagine a world where a person experiencing addiction can sit down and begin with: “Help me understand what could be happening.” Instead of: “Tell me why I am bad.” Imagine recovery systems where lived experience, pharmacology, genetics, environment, trauma, behavior, metabolism, and social context can be examined together rather than forced into competing silos. Imagine people arriving at professional care better able to: describe what happened; recognize patterns; communicate uncertainty; ask informed questions; identify contradictions; understand the difference between evidence and anecdote. That is the world the Recovery Kernel is trying to help build. ⚠️ Important Safety Notice The Recovery Kernel is an educational, open-source, and community resource framework. It does not replace: emergency medical services; physicians; pharmacists; mental-health professionals; addiction specialists; laboratory testing; individualized diagnosis or treatment. Some project materials discuss substances, withdrawal, interactions, experimental compounds, and recovery. Withdrawal from certain substances can be medically dangerous. Suspected overdose, severe withdrawal, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, seizure, severe confusion, or other acute medical emergencies require immediate professional assistance. United States emergency and crisis resources Emergency Services: 911 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Call or text 988 SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-4357 Crisis Text Line: Text HOME to 741741 Outside the United States, contact the appropriate emergency or crisis service in your country. 📬 Contact JR Token — The Architect Email: jr.token.thearchitect@gmail.com Audiobooks: https://www.youtube.com/@J.R.Token.TheArchitect Project Support: https://buymeacoffee.com/jrtoken 🙏 Acknowledgments The Recovery Kernel exists because of contributions from many forms of knowledge: people with lived experience; recovery advocates; researchers; neuroscientists; developers; data scientists; translators; harm-reduction practitioners; families; community health workers; accessibility advocates; open-source communities; and the people who kept asking questions after simple answers failed them. This work is also a product of an unusual collaboration between human observation, software engineering, structured knowledge systems, and multiple artificial-intelligence models. The project is intended to remain open to criticism, correction, iteration, and improvement. 🧬 THE RECOVERY KERNEL People are not error messages. Behavior has architecture. Architecture can be studied. Understanding can replace shame. When people understand their architecture, they can stop interpreting every struggle as a character defect. When shame loses its grip, curiosity becomes possible. When curiosity becomes possible, people can begin rebuilding. The Kernel is not a cure. It is not a treatment. It is not a protocol. It is a framework for understanding. And understanding is the beginning of everything. THE RECOVERY KERNEL OPEN SOURCE · FORKABLE · GLOBAL · BIAS-AWARE · HUMAN-FIRST Explore. Learn. Question. metadata.description: • La búsqueda del metal de los dioses: El episodio narra la trepidante carrera contra la organización Nexus por localizar la Nave Real Gaulós, un pecio fenicio del año 580 aC cargado de oricalco, una aleación legendaria tan valiosa que los antiguos la vinculaban con la Atlántida. • Tecnología de vanguardia y espionaje global: Acompaña al equipo de la Fundación Barrows en una misión que utiliza desde la constelación de satélites "Icarus", capaces de leer matrículas desde el espacio, hasta el hackeo de redes sismográficas para tesoros triangulares en el fondo marino. • Persecución en tres continentes: La trama se despliega desde los paisajes marcianos de las Minas de Riotinto en Huelva y la Nápoles sumergida, pasando por el lujo corrupto de Mykonos hasta las peligrosas aguas de la Triple Frontera en Sudamérica. • Inmersión extrema y ciencia ficción real: Descubre el desafío de bajar a 600 metros de profundidad mediante la ventilación líquida, una técnica experimental donde los protagonistas deben dejar de respirar aire para llenar sus pulmones de fluido oxigenado y sobrevivir a la presión del abismo. • El legado que reescribe la historia: El verdadero hallazgo de Tarsis no resulta ser el oro, sino una biblioteca sumergida con mapas de navegación que prueban que los fenicios llegaron a América mil años antes que Colón.

metadata.description: The Allen Atlas of the adult mouse brain is a brain-wide, genome-wide data set that has been made available online, triggering a renaissance in neuroanatomy. In particular, it has been used to define brain regions in a computational, data-driven way, and to estimate the region-specificity of cell types characterized independently by their transcriptional activity. However, these results were based on one series of co-registered (coronal) ISH image series per gene, whereas the online ABA contains several image series per genes, including sagittal ones. Since the sagittal series cover mostly the left hemisphere, we can simulate the variability of results by repeatedly drawing a random image series for each gene and restricting the computation to the left hemisphere. This gives rise to an estimate of error bars on the results of computational neuroanatomy.

metadata.description: At incident powers much higher than the threshold for filamentation a pulse from a high-power laser generates in the transversal plane a complex structure. It consists of randomly meandering stripes defining connected regions where the field intensity is high; and, the complementary regions dominated by diffusive plasma with defocusing property. The pattern is similar to an ensemble of clusters of various extensions. We provide evidence that there is a correlation between this filamentation and the {\it labyrinth} instability in reaction-diffusion systems. Besides the similarity of the spatial organization in the two cases, we show that the differential equations that describe these two dynamical processes lead to effects that can be mutually mapped. For the laser beam at high power the Non-linear Schrodinger Equation in a regime of strong self-focusing and ionization of the air leads to multiple filamentation and the structure of clusters. Under the effect of the {\it labyrinth} instability a model of activator-inhibitor leads to a similar pattern. The origin of this connection must be found in the fact that both optical turbulence and the activator-inhibitor dynamics have the nature of competition between two phases of the same system.

metadata.description: This research investigates the oft-criticised segment of the vocational education and training (VET) sector in Australia--private, for-profit registered training organisations (RTOs)--with the aim of gaining a clearer understanding of the approaches they adopt in training 15 to 19-year-olds who have left school early. Through a nationwide survey of private RTOs and a series of consultations with providers and industry stakeholders in Victoria, South Australia, and Queensland, the authors set out to reveal the nature of training provided by private RTOs to those young people seeking to complete their initial qualification, and the ways by which they respond to the needs of their young learners. On the basis of the findings, changes are considered that may be needed in order to improve the training outcomes for this growing cohort of learners. The research is set against a background of federal, state, and territory-based training entitlement regimes, which ensure a greater role for the VET sector in supporting the initial qualification attainment of young Australians. It has also been undertaken at a time when state and national governments are promoting a marketised and, consequently, highly competitive provider environment, prompted largely by the 2012 National Agreement for Skills and Workforce Development and the National Partnership Agreement on Skills Reform. These initiatives saw an expansion in both the number of private RTOs accessing government-funding, which now comprise approximately 3000 of Australia's 4200 registered training providers, and the number of private RTOs delivering vocational education to early school leavers. In this context a convergence of two trends was observed: (1) a high number of private RTOs that often lack the infrastructure, economies of scale, and student supports found in TAFE (technical and further education) institutions; and (2) a high number of young early school leavers relying on such providers to help them to renew or continue their education. While the numbers of young people undertaking vocational education have increased, the completion rates of publicly subsidised courses remain very low. Data from the National Centre for Vocational Education Research (NCVER) indicate that, for those aged under 25 years in full-time study with no prior post school qualification, the estimated completion rate is 51.6% (NCVER 2016). This suggests that catering to the needs of young people in VET--across all provider types and settings--remains a significant challenge. It is for this reason that the focus is on the private RTOs, who now represent a prominent segment of the VET landscape. The following are appended: (1) Survey Instrument; (2) Sample Provider Profiles; (3) Semi-Structured Interview Instrument: Private RTOs; and (4) Semi-Structured Interview Instrument: Other Stakeholders.
